evidence_policy.closed_verified: The defect's intended behavior was exercised by a regression or qualification gate; a later release delta did not invalidate that evidence.
evidence_policy.partial_residual: The primary defect was mitigated or one path was repaired, but the audit documents a remaining path, semantic mismatch, or robustness gap.
evidence_policy.accepted_limitation: The behavior is intentionally retained or observational and is not scheduled as a correctness repair.
evidence_policy.deferred_architecture: The item is structural debt rather than a release-local numerical defect.
evidence_policy.inference: Outside the two listed Channel-pressure files, rc2 residual findings remain applicable to rc3 unless a fresh reproducer closes them. This is an inference from the exact v0.2.0rc2..v0.2.0rc3 changed-file set.

work_queue.goal: Align Plane free-slip Nyquist handling with the qualified Periodic and Channel Stokes conventions.
Version actual dynamics and remove non-dynamical device or initialization details from restart identity.
Resolve or explicitly restrict the nonconvergent wall molecular-field representation and whole-slab initial taper.
Unify pressure stopping precedence, scale handling, diagnostics, and declarations.
Close remaining validation, diagnostics, permission, atomicity, and global-state inconsistencies.
Reduce drift by consolidating combination registration, checkpoint I/O, stepping, PCG, canonicalization, and import boundaries.

items.summary: Periodic full-complex state lacked Hermitian repair.
Channel dealiasing could leave the velocity field non-solenoidal.
Plane compiled_v2 rejected valid float32 configurations and left partial output.
Periodic and Channel saved hydrodynamics one step later than Q.
Plane free-slip Stokes now applies the qualified even-grid Nyquist convention consistently across full-complex and Hermitian-half storage.
Unsupported node-centered layouts were silently ignored.
Checkpoint integrity was hardened, but downgrade, path, filename, and extra-key edge cases remain.
Static lifting still represents a nonzero wall molecular-field contribution in a basis that does not converge at the wall.
Anchoring normals are validated, but the accepted sign convention is stricter than Q physics requires and diagnostics remain weak.
Historical functional identities are not frozen independently enough to survive future identity evolution.
TF32 policy coverage and restoration of caller global state are inconsistent across runtime paths.
Boolean and SHA options were accepted through permissive coercion.
Device and pressure validation remains inconsistent between Plane, legacy Channel, Periodic, and complete-stress Channel.
Restart save_start_step was compared against added steps instead of absolute progress.
Diagnostics schemas and persistence differ across the four public application families.
Spectral refresh declarations used incompatible disabled representations.
Capability catalog, compiler rejection, and public exception translation are not fully aligned.
Plane restart generated unrelated fresh-initial-condition artifacts.
Lifted Plane metadata described the wrong physical and remainder boundary conditions.
Fresh lifted initial-state conditioning uses a sine envelope over the whole slab rather than a localized wall transition.
Robin roots are robust for the intended range, but extreme symmetric impedance remains unsupported.
Plane runtime identity still contains the requested device token and can reject physically compatible restarts.
Non-CUDA indexed device tokens were not normalized consistently with allocated tensors.
Checkpoint mismatch and filesystem failures use inconsistent public exception classes.
Channel pressure-adjoint scaling does not robustly account for global vector norm and grid size at extreme magnitudes.
Functional runtime identities could not be copied, pickled, or replaced safely.
Checkpoint writers do not share atomic publication, permissions, and umask behavior.
Channel functional declarations retain stale executable and adjoint capability metadata.
Fixed-iteration and tolerance/max-iteration pressure policies can be contradictory without enforced precedence or postcondition.
Robin boundary_residual is constructionally near zero and is not an independent correctness gate.
Unsupported Channel snapshot initialization compiled successfully and failed only at runtime.
SBDF2 is a valid declaration type but unsupported combinations reject it at compilation.
Numerical and output defaults differed by entry point; rc2 made them explicit and rc3 completed the independent Consumer migration.
Public Output could not drive legacy Channel workflows.
Shendruk activity parameter round-trip differs by one floating-point ulp.
Even-grid Channel functional pressure transpose omitted production Nyquist projection.
The explicit public declarations introduced in rc2 broke all five PSSolver-Control constructors.
Corrected even-grid Channel dynamics were not represented by an explicit checkpoint/runtime dynamics version.
The partial lifting repair worsened a twisted-profile velocity convergence case and ignored a declared molecular-field-space option.
Lifted rc1 checkpoints are rejected by initial-conditioning identity rather than an explicit dynamics version.
Full-complex Hermitian projection metadata and checkpoint identity do not describe the actual repaired dynamics.
Each model-geometry combination duplicates an eight-module application stack.
Checkpoint implementations and integrity helpers are duplicated across production and functional paths.
Functional API compatibility, validation, versioning, and exception layers are oversized and overlapping.
Semi-implicit updates, spectral refresh, advance, and progress restoration are duplicated.
Four Channel PCG loops implement different stopping and breakdown rules.
Robin and finite-Q pilots span many production layers while no public application is qualified.
Canonical JSON, hashing, identifiers, and validation helpers are repeatedly reimplemented.
Qualification records and benchmark harnesses duplicate provenance and atomic-output infrastructure.
Import-boundary ratchets do not cover newer functional, API, boundary, and diagnostics layers.
